problem:
Crestfield Bank, a fictional bank, offers instant US dollar payments to customers in several corridors. The FX rate is competitive, the customer experience is smooth, and the marketing promises instant settlement. Yet on some mornings the payments fail or sit in a queue, and the treasury team discovers the cause only after customers complain: the bank does not hold enough US dollars in the right nostro account at the right time to settle the payments it has accepted.

The product team confuses two different things. FX conversion changes one currency into another at a rate. Liquidity is whether the settlement currency is actually available in the right account at the required time. A payment can have a perfect rate and still be unable to settle, because the dollars are in the wrong account, the correspondent is closed, or the nostro balance is committed to other payments.

Crestfield Bank must distinguish FX conversion from availability of settlement currency at the required time, and design routing, liquidity checks and fallbacks so the bank only promises what its liquidity position can deliver.
solution:
Check liquidity as a first class step in the payment flow, not as an afterthought in treasury. Before the bank promises an instant outcome, the payment engine must confirm the settlement currency balance in the correct nostro or settlement account, the correspondent availability, the cut off and the value date. That check uses live positions, not yesterday's balance, and it reserves the funds for the payment so a later payment cannot consume the same dollars.

Route with liquidity in mind. The routing service must evaluate eligibility, currency, country, service, cut off, cost and liquidity together, using current effective dated reference data. If the primary correspondent is unavailable or no longer supports the required currency or route, the engine re-evaluates against the same criteria and uses an approved alternate route only if policy permits. Otherwise it queues or rejects the payment with a transparent reason. It must never silently change the beneficiary, the settlement details or the rate to make a route fit.

Validate the full correspondent chain before release. Each intermediary must support the currency, the country and the service, and each relationship must be current on the effective date. A chain with a missing or expired link is excluded, and the payment is held for repair or routed through an approved alternative. Routing decisions are recorded with the factors that produced them, so an analyst can explain why a payment took one route and not another.

Give treasury a live view and the customer an honest one. Treasury monitors nostro balances, committed reservations, intraday liquidity usage and corridor demand, with alerts before a corridor runs short. The customer sees a realistic timing promise, and a payment that cannot settle instantly is held or queued with a clear status rather than shown as complete.

decision.question: Crestfield Bank has accepted 200 instant US dollar payments for a corridor where the nostro balance covers only 120 of them. The FX rates are all locked and valid. What should the bank do with the remaining 80 payments?

options.label: A
options.detail: Hold or queue the remaining payments under a documented rule, tell the affected customers the realistic timing, and use an approved alternate route or liquidity source only where policy permits.

options.label: B
options.detail: Change the FX rate on the remaining 80 to cover the shortfall.

options.label: C
options.detail: Cancel all 200 payments and start again tomorrow.

options.label: D
options.detail: Send all 200 anyway and hope the nostro is topped up before settlement.

decisionRationale: Option A is correct because liquidity must be checked before settlement is promised, and a shortfall is handled by a governed hold, queue or approved alternate route with transparent customer communication. Option D is wrong because sending without cover creates settlement failure. Option B is wrong because changing a locked rate without consent breaks the quote contract. Option C is wrong because it penalises the 120 payments that can settle.

steps.title: Submits an instant US dollar payment in the channel
Validates the instruction and checks the FX quote and customer limits
Evaluates eligible correspondents against currency, country, service, cut off and liquidity data
Confirms and reserves the settlement currency in the correct nostro account
Runs sanctions, AML and fraud screening
Builds the pacs.008 or pacs.009 message with the validated correspondent chain
Submits the message through the selected correspondent and records the settlement instruction
Confirms settlement or releases the reservation and notifies the customer

happy: The customer submits a US dollar payment, routing selects an eligible correspondent with sufficient nostro liquidity, the funds are reserved, screening passes, the message is sent through the validated chain, settlement completes, the reservation converts to a final posting, and the customer sees a confirmed completion.

negative.title: Correspondent unavailable
negative.detail: The selected correspondent is temporarily unavailable or no longer supports the currency or route. Re-evaluate routing against current data, use an approved alternate route only if policy permits, otherwise queue or reject with a transparent reason.

negative.title: Liquidity insufficient
negative.detail: The nostro balance cannot cover the payment at the required time. Hold or queue the payment under the documented rule, alert treasury, and tell the customer the realistic timing rather than promising instant settlement.

negative.title: Missing or outdated correspondent data
negative.detail: The chain lacks a valid intermediary or a relationship has expired. Exclude the invalid route, hold the payment for repair or select an approved alternative, and record the data gap for reference data governance.

negative.title: Wrong intermediary selected
negative.detail: The payment is routed through an intermediary that cannot serve the destination or currency. Trace the route decision, compare it with routing policy and reference data, correct the rule or the data, and hold affected payments for re-routing.

technical: Hold nostro positions, reservations and committed amounts as live data with a correlation ID per payment, and enforce reservation as an atomic step so two payments cannot reserve the same funds. Version all routing reference data with effective dates and record the version used for each routing decision, including the factors that produced it. Validate BICs, agent sequences, currency support and country restrictions before release, and keep the routing decision, the liquidity check and the screening outcome as structured audit events. Make settlement posting idempotent so a late confirmation cannot post twice, and reconcile nostro movements against payment instructions intraday.

accounting: Debit the customer account and reserve the settlement currency in the nostro account at instruction time, then convert the reservation to a final nostro debit on settlement confirmation. If the payment is queued or rejected for liquidity, release the reservation exactly once and restore the customer balance where a debit was taken. Nostro reconciliation runs intraday against correspondent statements, and any break goes to a treasury worklist with an ageing service level. Treasury monitors nostro balances by currency and corridor, reservation ageing and alternate route usage, and sets intraday limits so one corridor cannot consume liquidity needed elsewhere. For context on US instant limits, FedNow and RTP each carry a USD 10 million maximum, so the constraint in this case is the bank's own nostro position, not the scheme limit.

questions.question: What is the difference between FX conversion and settlement currency availability?
options: Availability is only about the rate
Conversion sets the rate; availability is whether the settlement currency is in the right account at the required time
questions.explanation: A good rate does not settle a payment if the settlement currency is not available when and where it is needed.

questions.question: What should happen when the primary correspondent is unavailable?
options: Re-evaluate routing and use an approved alternate only if policy permits, otherwise queue or reject transparently
Change the beneficiary to fit the route
questions.explanation: Routing must be re-evaluated against current eligibility, currency, country, service, cut off, cost and liquidity data.

questions.question: What is the FedNow maximum, effective November 2025?
questions.explanation: The FedNow maximum is USD 10 million effective November 2025, with a participant default of USD 100,000.

questions.question: Why must a routing decision record its decision factors?
options: So an analyst can explain why one route was chosen and prove it was valid for the currency and date
questions.explanation: Explainable routing decisions with effective dated reference data are needed for control, investigation and audit.
